The losses of Linderbaum and Rutschman underscore the need for salary cap in all sports.

Linderbaum loss is a very good player who was bought away from the Ravens.  The price was one they wisely avoided paying within a structure where all teams are playing by the same rules.  Sucks to lose him, but the cap can be better deployed.

Rutschman trade is probably an overpay by the Red Sox as well both in terms of prospects and what they'll have to pay him in terms of his new contract, but it's an insect bite to the Red Sox who can simply fill any holes on the open market like the Dodgers or Yankees.

Baseball needs a salary cap (a floor makes sense as well) and I'm at the point where I don't care how much baseball we need to lose to a lockout to get it done.

The owners need to hold the line on this, not for themselves, but for the game and its fans.  A competitive 30-team league can make baseball flourish again.
